note: Programmatic input schemas for the twenty-one interactive tools. Agents replicate each tool's logic by feeding these inputs to the documented formulas / shipped JS (assets/js/<id>.js); the UI pages are the human front-end for the same logic.

tools.title: Niche Picker

q3.description: Max money per view, biggest audience, or balance.

The 2027 branch scores the 20 atlas niches against data/niches.json outlook_2027 trajectories (heating +3 / stable +1 / cooling -2), growth-signal matches, format fit, risk alignment, and atlas skill_fit — OUTLOOK_2027 in quiz.js mirrors the JSON and tests/niche-atlas.test.js checks sync.

tools.title: Revenue Calculator
tools.description: Project revenue from views, niche, sponsors, and affiliates — with honest ranges.

niche.description: Must be a key of calculators.json youtube_longform_rpm_bands.

avg_sponsor_video_views.description: Expected views on the sponsored video(s).

tools.output: Monthly revenue range [lo, hi] split into long-form ads, Shorts ads, sponsorships, affiliate/products, plus annualized totals. Ranges, never promises.
tools.drive_notes: Math (assets/js/calculator.js): long-form ads = views/1000 × RPM band from calculators.json; Shorts ads = shorts/1000 × shorts_rpm_per_1000; sponsorships = deals × (sponsor views/1000) × sponsorship_rule_of_thumb.dedicated_cpm_range; affiliate = input × 0.7–1.3.

tools.title: The Deal Analyzer
tools.description: Paste the brand's terms — rate-card verdict with platform multipliers + niche adjustment, the wave-22 contract checklist applied to the deal, counter-offer calculator, 2026 usage-rights add-on math, deal history + comparison mode.

deliverable.description: Integrated slot, dedicated video, or short-form video.

niche.description: Optional — adjusts the verdict range by the niche multiplier (finance/tech x2.5, entertainment/gaming/music x0.6) and enables the AIR category-CPM cross-check where mapped.

expected_views.description: If known, enables the implied-CPM check and the category-CPM cross-check.

post_count.description: Posts in the bundle — 3+ triggers the 15-20% bundle-discount guidance.

contract.description: Ten contract-language answers feeding the wave-22 checklist.

tools.output: Verdict (UNDERPAID / FAIR / STRONG) against the niche-adjusted benchmark range, implied CPM vs rate-card CPMs, AIR category-CPM cross-check (where mapped), offer-term flags, wave-22 contract checklist verdict (clean / caution / dont_sign) with per-flag fixes, counter-offer with line-item ranges + open-ended totals, usage-rights add-on table, plaintext export.
tools.drive_notes: Engine (assets/js/deal-analyzer.js, UMD — require() it in node): DealAnalyzer.validInput() normalizes; .evaluate(deal, rateCard) returns the tier range x niche multiplier (parity-pinned with the simulator's sponsorNicheMult), verdict, implied CPM, categoryCheck (AIR Oct-2026 category CPMs: finance/real-estate $58, B2B SaaS/AI $46.50, health $28, gaming/tech $18.50, entertainment $14), cross-platform ranges + the 1.7x/0.85x note, and the 23%-benchmark expected close; .offerTermFlags() scans usage/whitelisting/exclusivity/payment/timeline; .mapTermsToFlags() + .contractRisk(flagIds, deal-templates.json contract_flags) apply the wave-22 checklist (walk_away = dont_sign, major 2pts, minor 1pt, 3+ = dont_sign — same scoring as Outreach.contractRisk); .usageAddons() prices the 2026 benchmark ranges (3mo +25-50%, 3-6mo +50-75%, 6-12mo +75-100%, perpetual from 2x; whitelisting 30-100%/mo) from calculators.json usage_rights_benchmarks_2026 (calculators v1.5.0); .counterOffer() builds base + line items + open-ended totals + the 15-20% bundle guidance; .exportReport() renders the plaintext evaluation; .compareDeals() diffs two saved deals. Browser history/compare/print live in assets/js/deal-analyzer-ui.js (localStorage only). Negotiation aid — not financial, legal, or tax advice; the checklist is not legal advice. See AGENT.md Workflow 12.

tools.title: The Deal Room
tools.description: Deal Room 2.0: track offers through signing against the niche-adjusted 2026 rate card, read the pipeline totals, price usage rights, check real quoted prices, read the Algorithm Watch digest, export your memo.

niche.description: Optional sponsor niche key (same table as the Deal Analyzer / simulator sponsorNicheMult) — adjusts the benchmark range the offer is scored against.

expected_views.description: Last-10-video average; the number sponsors buy.

timeline.description: Due date / delivery window as written in the offer.

status.description: Where the deal sits in the offer → paid pipeline.

tools.output: Tracked deal records with niche-adjusted rate-card verdicts (UNDERPAID / FAIR / STRONG + the ~23% listed-vs-accepted note), a pipeline summary over the creator's own logged deals (stage totals, committed vs paid, underpaid deals still in play), the full 2026 rate-card table with reported vs modeled bases kept separate, a quoted-price check against real negotiation data, usage-rights line-item pricing (reported +50/+75/+100% band; no invented whitelisting/buyout multipliers), per-situation negotiation scripts, interactive red-flag checklist scoring, the Algorithm Watch digest (dated, sourced, confidence-flagged, with per-entry deal notes), and a one-page deal memo.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/deal-room.js, UMD — importable in node): scoreOffer(offer, lo, hi) benchmarks against sponsorship_rate_card_2026; scoreDeal(deal, rateCard) adds the niche multiplier (parity-pinned with DealAnalyzer.nicheMult) + implied CPM; rateCardTable(rateCard, quoted) returns the full tier table + multipliers + CPMs + the quoted-prices block; quotedPriceCheck(deal, quoted) reads sponsorship_quoted_prices_2026 (calculators.json v1.5.0 — Cheerful Sep-2026 reported asks/quotes; Click Analytic 2026 Instagram model, labeled modeled) and returns null where no format is honestly mapped; pipelineSummary(deals, rateCard) totals the creator's own pipeline with no invented close probabilities; watchDigest(feed, {days, limit, now}) + digestText(digest) build the Algorithm Watch digest from data/v1/changes.json with curated per-entry deal notes (editorial, labeled); priceUsage(baseFee, tierId, usage_rights_tiers) applies the reported multipliers, returning guidance instead of numbers for whitelisting/buyout; redFlagScore(checkedIds, red_flags) scores contract structure (any walk_away flag or 3+ points -> walk away); renderScript(script, vars) fills {{placeholders}}; dealMemo(deal, scored, flags) builds the one-page record. Scripts + checklist + tiers live in data/v1/deal-templates.json. Negotiation aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: Hiring Cost Calculator
tools.description: Price your first hire: monthly/annual cost and the ad revenue needed to cover it — honest math, no promises.

role.description: Video editor, thumbnail designer, virtual assistant, channel manager/ops.

billing_model.description: hourly = rate/hr × hours/week; per_video = rate × units/month; monthly = retainer.

monthly_views.description: Your current monthly long-form views, for the coverage math.

tools.output: Monthly/annual cost (sticker vs +15% loaded), share of ad revenue, monthly views needed to cover the loaded cost, 3-month coverage reserve.
tools.drive_notes: Math (assets/js/hiring-calculator.js): hourly → rate × hrs × 52/12; per_video → rate × units; monthly → retainer. Loaded cost = sticker × 1.15 (management, revisions, fees). Coverage views = loaded ÷ RPM band × 1000 (both band ends). The hiring rule: cover 3 months from revenue before signing.

Enforce native grammar — no watermarks, no copy-paste. 2.0 adds the full derivative map via ContentEngine.repurposeMap (7 derivatives: short clip, community reaction, TikTok cut, Reel cut, newsletter issue, X thread, Facebook post) — every derivative carries a required original element (repurposing is not re-uploading) plus the Oct-1 originality guardrails (ContentEngine.originalityGuardrails). Machine-readable map + guardrails: data/v1/content-engine.json repurposing_2_0 / originality_guardrails.

tools.title: Empire Simulator
tools.description: Simulate 12–36 months of channel growth + revenue — the 10 real 2026 study niches (TubeAI/AIR medians + labeled RPM bands), niche/cadence/quality sliders, platform mix (Shorts/TikTok/Reels under their real 2026 rules), 12-scenario library, A/B comparison, team hiring P&L, what-if event cards, Money Map stage transitions, the “what would it take?” goal solver, live re-run, the mission-control launch sequence, and the animated watch-the-empire-build chart with milestone celebrations + kind reality checks — a model, not a prediction.

niche.description: The 10 real 2026 study niches (TubeAI/AIR Sep 2026). Each sets the niche_rpm_2026 RPM band (labeled reported/proxy/CPM-reported) and shows the study median as context for monthly_growth_rate — the median is never a multiplier.

publish_tiktok.description: Arm TikTok: the short-form output is split across Shorts/TikTok/Reels (normalized shares). TikTok pays Creator Rewards on ~50% of raw views (qualifying views) at $0.40-$2.00/1k past the 10K-follower gate; under the gate it pays $0.

publish_reels.description: Arm Instagram Reels: takes a real share of the short-form output and pays $0/view (2026) — the honest number, modeled explicitly. Reels build audience monetized elsewhere.

short_mix.description: Raw platform weights {shorts, tiktok, reels}; normalized across armed platforms. Defaults 60/25/15.

monthly_growth_rate.description: Base monthly compounding growth at reference cadence (assumption, adjustable).

scenario_id.description: One-click preset: loads a full named starting config from the engine's SCENARIOS library (research-sourced assumptions).

horizon.description: 12, 24, or 36 months. 24 adds year-2 diminishing returns (monthly growth decays x0.94/mo after month 12); 36 adds year-3 (x0.97/mo after month 24) plus Money Map stage transitions — the engine's labeled curves.

type.description: First-Hire-guide role: editor, thumbnail designer, or virtual assistant.

monthly_cost_usd.description: Omit to use the guide preset: editor $1,400, thumbnail $120, VA $900.

hires.description: Team hires: each adds output/quality lift and subtracts monthly cost (month-by-month P&L: gross, team cost, net). First active month at 50% effect (ramp-up).

id.description: What-if event card: algorithm-change (Shorts reach cut), viral-hit (one video 10x's), burnout-break (2 months off), policy-change (Feb-2027 YPP rules), holiday-shopping-surge (Q4 affiliate windfall).

start_month.description: The month the card lands on the timeline.

events.description: What-if event cards: random-but-transparent scenario events with chapter-cited assumed effects. algorithm-change: Shorts views x0.6 from the card month (Oct-1-2026 originality update). viral-hit: event month long views x10, one-time +8% subs, next month x1.5 tail (reality check built in: virality spikes views, not loyalty). burnout-break: 2 months of zero growth, -0.5%/mo subs drift, views x0.3. policy-change: the Feb-2027 10M-qualified-Shorts-views/90d revenue floor — Shorts ads pay $0 in months under it. holiday-shopping-surge: the event month + the next month, affiliate revenue x1.8 (the two-month holiday buying window — TikTok Shop BFCM 2025 $500M/4 days, Adobe 2026 holiday forecast). Multipliers are the engine's labeled assumptions, never platform data.

compare_with.description: A/B mode: {name_b, inputs_b} — compare(nameA, inputsA, nameB, inputsB, cfg) runs both over the same horizon and returns B-minus-A deltas plus a plain-language verdict.

name_b.description: Label for the B path (e.g. 'Tech reviewer').

inputs_b.description: Full SimulatorInput for the B path (or a scenario_id).

tools.output: 12-, 24-, or 36-month projection: subs, views, and revenue per month per stream (ads, sponsors, affiliates, digital), month-by-month team P&L (gross, team cost, net), per-month Money Map stage (0-4 from monthly net + team) with the stage-transition timeline, active what-if event cards per month, totals, milestones, and the full named-assumptions list. compare() adds side-by-side deltas (B minus A) and a verdict. exportPlan() renders the copy-my-empire-plan text incl. the stage journey. A model, not a prediction.
tools.drive_notes: Engine (assets/js/sim-engine.js, UMD — importable in node): simulate(inputs, cfg) with cfg = calculators.json. scenarioInputs(id) loads a named preset from the SCENARIOS library (12 presets, research-sourced assumptions); compare(nameA, inputsA, nameB, inputsB, cfg) runs two configs over the same clock (deltas are B minus A); assumptionLines(inputs, res) is the always-visible assumptions panel; exportPlan(scenarioName, inputs, res) renders the share text; normalizeEvents() validates the 5 what-if cards; stageForNet(net, teamActive) is the single source of the 0-4 stage rule; solveForGoal(inputs, cfg, {target: "subs"|"net"|"stage", value, month, variable: "growth"|"cadence"}) binary-searches base growth (whole %) or long-form cadence (half videos) until the target lands by the month — pure inversion of simulate(), no new claims (see AGENT.md Workflow 13). The 4.0 UI adds live re-run (debounced), stage-banded subscriber charts with milestone/event markers, year cards, and an always-visible assumptions block. Wow wave 2 flagship: the 10 study niches carry real TubeAI/AIR medians as CONTEXT (never multipliers) + labeled RPM bands from calculators.json niche_rpm_2026 (reported/proxy/CPM-reported). Growth compounds monthly x cadence x quality (diminishing, capped 2.5x). Hires add output/quality and subtract cost monthly (first active month at 50% ramp). Year-2 decays growth x0.94/mo after month 12; year-3 x0.97/mo after month 24 (growth stays positive — plateau, not collapse). RPMs come from calculators.json niche_rpm_2026 (the 10 study niches; legacy scenario keys still read youtube_longform_rpm_bands). Platform mix: publish_tiktok/publish_reels split the short-form output across Shorts/TikTok/Reels (normalized); TikTok pays Creator Rewards on ~50% of raw views at $0.40-$2.00/1k past the 10K gate; Reels pay $0/view. realityChecks(inputs, res) returns the kind hard truths (<1% to 100K, hyper-growth, kids-trap, reels-zero, tiktok-gate, ads-vs-sponsors). moneyMapToInputs(answers) feeds the Money Map quiz into starting stats. Every assumption is named in DEFAULTS and listed on-page. Wow wave 1 adds the mission-control launch sequence (assets/js/simulator-launch.js, UMD pure helpers + DOM): explicit runs fly pre-flight checks (four real gates), a T-minus countdown, mission elapsed-time telemetry streamed month-by-month, then the full results plus a stamped MISSION DEBRIEF that credits +25 XP to the Empire Climb journal (shared localStorage store with the Money Map). Live-update re-runs bypass the sequence; reduced-motion/calm users get checks + debrief + XP without the motion; ABORT/Esc scrubs before anything is computed.

tools.description: Film-day math: does your shoot capacity actually cover your cadence? Honest surplus/shortfall, consistency-beats-volume framing.

videos_per_shoot_day.description: Long-form videos filmed per shoot day (honest average).

shoot_days_per_month.description: Scheduled, repeatable shoot days — 'I'll find the time' doesn't count.

publish_tiktok.description: Arm TikTok: the short-form output is split across Shorts/TikTok/Reels (normalized shares). TikTok pays Creator Rewards on ~50% of raw views (qualifying views) at $0.40-$2.00/1k past the 10K-follower gate; under the gate it pays $0.

publish_reels.description: Arm Instagram Reels: takes a real share of the short-form output and pays $0/view (2026) — the honest number, modeled explicitly. Reels build audience monetized elsewhere.

short_mix.description: Raw platform weights {shorts, tiktok, reels}; normalized across armed platforms. Defaults 60/25/15.

task_minutes.description: Scheduler: per-task minutes {long:{film,edit,publish}, short:{film,edit,publish}} — your own timings; blanks fall back to starting estimates.

tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/content-engine.js, UMD — importable in node): batchingMath(opts) — capacity = shoot_days_per_month × videos_per_shoot_day; required = cadence × 52/12 (the honest month); verdict surplus/balanced/shortfall with guidance text. 2.0 adds planBatchWeek({weeklyHours, longsPerWeek, shortsPerWeek, restDay, taskMinutes}) — weekly hours blocked into film/edit/publish day-blocks (8h/day cap, rest day untouched); verdict holds/tight/over with lever guidance. Defaults for task minutes are adjustable starting estimates, not benchmarks. Pure arithmetic on the creator's own inputs — never a promise. Planning aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

revenue.description: Typical monthly content revenue band. The honest anchor: placement is driven by this, not by audience or team size.

streams.description: Revenue streams actually paying right now.

Placement anchored on the creator's own reported revenue band; stages are focus guides, never income promises.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/money-map.js, UMD — importable in node): placeStage(a) — revenue band maps 0→0, 1-99→1, 100-999→2, 1k-9999→3, 10k-plus→4; if audience is 100k+ and base stage ≤ 2, stage+1 with an 'audience-ahead' note; employees with stage ≤ 2 adds a 'team-ahead' note. roadmap(a) — stage signature move (the stage's #1 tool) + two bottleneck-driven moves, deduped. STAGES carries the full playbook data (goal, 3 moves, trap, graduate). Wow wave 1 adds the Empire Climb: RANKS (RECRUIT/CADET/OPERATIVE/COMMANDER/GENERAL, chevron insignias), RANK_THRESHOLDS [0,100,275,500,775], XP_AWARDS {survey:50, move:25, stage:100, mission:25}; awardXP(store,key,amount,label) is idempotent per key, revokeKey undoes; rankFor/nextRankInfo map totals to ranks; loadClimb/saveClimb persist the cge.empireclimb.v1 journal (one-time migration from the pre-climb store). XP is a work journal — missions cleared, stages closed — never money earned; no rank promises revenue. Planning aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

Templates + contract flags from data/v1/deal-templates.json. Negotiation aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: Cross-Post Optimizer
tools.description: Take one clip to every platform without getting throttled: per-destination adaptation checklists (aspect, captions, hooks, CTAs, disclosure labels) under the Oct-1 originality rules.

destinations.description: Where it should go (the source is ignored if included).

photorealistic_ai.description: The clip uses photorealistic AI visuals — triggers the YouTube disclosure-label reminder (labeled = normal distribution; undisclosed = reduced recommendations or removal).

tools.output: Per-destination adaptation cards (aspect, captions, hook rework, CTA, audio, disclosure label, one-original-element changes) + the universal checks + the Oct-1 gate reminder. Adaptation guidance under the platforms' stated 2026 rules — never a promise of reach, views, or revenue.
tools.drive_notes: Engine (assets/js/content-engine.js, UMD — importable in node): adaptChecklist(source_platform, destinations) reads the adaptation matrix (12 source→destination rule sets + 6 universal checks); unknown platforms and the source itself are filtered out. Matrix + grammars + gate: data/v1/content-engine.json -> adaptation_matrix. Pairs with the content-repurposing skill. Planning aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: Cadence Coach
tools.description: How often should you actually post? Turn your honest weekly hours, formats, and platforms into a sustainable cadence — capacity math plus Oct-2026 platform realities. Consistency beats volume.

longMins.description: Minutes per long-form video (film+edit+publish); adjustable starting estimate.

shortMins.description: Minutes per short-form post (film+edit+publish); adjustable starting estimate.

stage.description: Money Map stage; 0 adds the tuition-phase caveat.

priority.description: Which format gets production minutes first.

overheadPct.description: Share of hours reserved for comments/admin/analytics.

tools.output: Recommended longs/week + shorts/week, utilization vs production time (holds/tight/over), a 7-day schedule grid (rest day empty), per-platform Oct-2026 revenue realities, the 2-week ramp suggestion, method notes. Capacity arithmetic only — never a promise of views, revenue, or growth.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/cadence.js, UMD): production minutes = weeklyHours*60*(1-overheadPct); longs-first/shorts-first/balanced-50-50 allocation by per-piece minutes; utilization = used/production minutes (holds ≤0.7, tight ≤0.95, over above); dealWeek() spreads longs evenly over non-rest days and round-robins shorts; platform notes are the Oct-11-2026 research facts (TikTok Rewards 1-min+ qualifier $0.40–$1.00/1K, Reels $0, Shorts $0.02–$0.20/1K + Feb-2027 10M floor + Oct-1 originality rule, 20M+ uploads/day). Planning aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: Format Fit Finder
tools.description: Six questions about the creator's real situation — experience, weekly hours, on-camera comfort, budget, monetization goal, risk tolerance — scored against the 10 breakout-format dossiers; ranked matches with why-it-fits reasoning, the catch, creator-reported pay ranges, and first 3 moves.

experience.description: The creator's real background; none-yet adds a tuition-phase note.

camera.description: On-camera comfort: face = loves camera, voice = voiceover only, hands = show work not face.

budget.description: Production budget tier: near $0, a few hundred for gear/tools, $500+/mo.

goal.description: Monetization timeline: under 6 months, 6–18 months, 18+ months.

tools.output: Ranked matches (score of 13, strong/workable/weak bands) with per-match why-it-fits reasoning, the honest catch from the dossier's risks, creator-reported pay ranges, competition, first 3 moves, per-match mismatch flags, global honesty flags, and the rate-card context. Matching arithmetic only — never a promise of views, revenue, or growth.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/format-fit.js, UMD): FORMATS mirrors data/niches.json v2.1.0 breakout_format_dossiers (id, dossier_no order, pay + competition labels — tests pin the sync); axis scores experience(3)/camera(2)/hours(2)/budget(2)/goal(2)/risk(2) = 13 max; camera-clash and hours-mismatch hard penalties; bands strong >=9, workable 6–8, weak <6; ties break by dossier order; global flags for none-yet, <3h/week, and fast-money-plus-play-it-safe. Planning aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: Deal Builder
tools.description: Turn deliverables into a line-item quote from the 2026 rate card: base fees per deliverable, usage rights, whitelisting, and exclusivity as stacked line items — plus a ready-to-send proposal built from the quote and a deal checklist built from the terms.

followers.description: Follower/subscriber count on the platform being sold (nano floor 1,000).

kind.description: dedicated = brand is the video; integrated = mid-roll slot; short = Short/TikTok/Reel; ugc = creative without posting (Storika UGC band).

deliverables.description: The package: each deliverable is its own line item.

viewsAvg.description: Last-10-video average views; sponsors buy views, not subs. Without it, integrated/short lines price at half the tier band (labeled fallback).

usage.description: Paid-ad usage tier from calculators.json usage_rights_benchmarks_2026.

whitelistingMonths.description: Months the brand runs ads from YOUR account (30–100%/mo of post-fee base).

scope.description: named = named competitors (+25% 30d / +50% 60–90d); category = broad lock, priced to cover lost deals or flagged.

commissionPct.description: Affiliate commission % on top of the flat fee — the bonus, not the deal.

tools.output: Line-item quote: per-deliverable lines (per-unit + line ranges with the data basis named), post-fee base, usage add-on (+25–50% / +50–75% / +75–100% / perpetual from 2x), whitelisting add-on (30–100%/mo), exclusivity add-on or broad-lock flag, package total, expected landing zone (~23% below the ask), bundle + multi-platform + honesty notes; exclusivity/usage-window conflict flags (walk_away/flag/note levels, incl. the can't-see-other-contracts honesty note); proposal email with unsupplied stats as [brackets] (never invented); 7-group deal checklist (usage, payment, revisions, exclusivity, FTC disclosure, deliverables, walk-away) customized to the quote's terms. All ranges and guidance, never promises.
tools.drive_notes: Engine (assets/js/deal-builder.js, UMD — importable in node): validInput() validates (followers ≥1,000, ≤8 deliverable lines, count 1–12, exclusivity consistency); tierOf() parity-pinned with Outreach.tierOf; deliverableBase() reads sponsorship_rate_card_2026 (dedicated = tier band, integrated/short = sponsored-CPM × viewsAvg with a labeled half-band fallback, ugc = Storika $150–$1,000 single-source); buildQuote() stacks base + usage (usage_rights_benchmarks_2026 tiers) + whitelisting (monthly) + exclusivity (named +25%/+50%, category flagged not invented) — 2-sig-fig rounding, expectedClose ×(1−0.23); exclusivityConflicts() checks window mismatches, perpetual+exclusivity, whitelisting-outliving-lock, UGC+affiliate edges; buildChecklist() generates the 7-group checklist from the quote; renderPitch() writes the proposal with [bracket] placeholders. Negotiation aid — not financial, legal, or tax advice; the checklist is not legal advice. See AGENT.md Workflow 14.
